item.title: Medicated deer feeders cut ticks until regulation ended them
item.description: On Shelter Island, four-poster feeders that treated deer with anti-tick chemicals as they ate corn cut the average nymph count in a single drag from 440 to 18 during the first three years of a Cornell study. The town's program effectively ended in 2020, when New York's Department of Environmental Conservation regulations required permission from every landowner within 745 feet of a feeder.

item.content:encoded: Scott Alexander surfaced the September essay in his Links for November 2026, saying it is either pretty devastating or implies natural law theorists are doing something very different from what he would expect moral philosophy to be. item.title: Let AI models reward-hack — just don't keep the weights — ACX Links
